The company is confirmed to be:
a) an incorporated business entity
b) in operation for at least 12 months
c) generating a majority of revenue from a competitive market.

The company does not fall into any of the following categories.
a) Business divisions, brands, or units, or businesses that are not complete and distinct from their parent or group of affiliates
b) Franchisors who do not own a majority of global franchisee locations, or franchisors without geographic distinction from independent franchisees
c) Non-profits or Civil Society Organizations (CSOs), foundations, or charitable entities, unless otherwise approved by B Lab
d) Governments, government agencies, government ministries, or state-owned enterprises, unless otherwise approved by B Lab
e) Company legally registered in regions not covered operationally by B Lab and not part of a larger group registered in a region covered by B Lab

The company generates less than 1% of annual revenue from direct involvement in the listed industries.
a) Fossil fuel producers
b) Gambling
c) Pornography
d) Prisons and detention centers (including prison or detention center labor)
e) Tobacco
f) Weapons

The company generates less than 1% of annual revenue from selling the following products or services to organizational clients in the listed industries (see Compliance Criterion 1.2.1).
a) Lobbying or public relations services
b) Marketing, advertising, or branding services
c) Physical products tailored for a client in a listed industry

The company generates less than 1% of annual revenue from direct growth financing in the listed industries (see Compliance Criterion 1.2.1) through the following activities.
a) Direct equity investments
b) Private equity, venture capital, or growth capital, including debt financing
For electric utilities and power generation companies, less than 50% of their product portfolio or energy mix is from fossil fuels.
B Corps certified against V1.6 of the standards must meet FR1.2 by Year 3 (not Year 0).
The company complies with all applicable local and national laws and regulations.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certification process.

The company shares accurate and complete information by:
a) using credible evidence and data source
b) having a clear understanding of B Lab’s resources.

The company shares accurate and complete information at all times:
a) in its B Impact Assessment
b) in providing information to assurance providers authorized by B Lab
c) in all communications with B Lab personnel.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certification process.
The company shares basic details for its B Corp public profile through the B Impact Assessment platform.
The company agrees to publicly share information as required by the B Lab Standard.
If the company is a wholly-owned or majority-owned subsidiary, or a large public company, it makes its entire B Impact Assessment report public and identifies any majority owners.

The company agrees that B Lab can make its B Impact Report and basic profile information available on the B Lab Global website and other B Lab and Sistema B Global Partner websites while the company is a certified B Corp.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certification process.

The company adopts an entity type or an amendment to its governing documents to require stakeholder governance (meaning it considers stakeholders in its decision-making). The company adopts stakeholder governance in accordance with the B Corp legal requirement, and as applicable to its legal form and jurisdiction.

If the company cannot adopt a stakeholder governance legal form because of local laws, it signs the B Corp Agreement and commits to:
a) working with B Lab to determine the appropriate legal pathway
b) advocating for benefit corporation legislation in its jurisdiction
c) amending its formation documents or adopting a new legal form if one is enacted through local lawmaking.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certification process.

The company commits to the shared collective purpose of the B Corp community, as set out in the Declaration of Interdependence:
We envision a global economy that uses business as a force for good. This economy is comprised of a new type of corporation — the B Corporation — which is purpose-driven and creates benefit for all stakeholders, not just shareholders.
As Certified B Corporations and leaders of this emerging economy, we believe:
That we must be the change we seek in the world.
That all business ought to be conducted as if people and place mattered.
That, through their products, practices, and profits, businesses should aspire to do no harm and benefit all.
To do so requires that we act with the understanding that we are each dependent upon another and thus responsible for each other and future generations.
The company signs an Agreement committing to the B Corp Certification process.
The company creates a risk profile using B Lab’s Risk Tool by answering the 14 questions in FR3.1.a to FR3.1.n.
The company meets any additional Impact Topic sub-requirements that the Risk Tool activates.
The company agrees to a summary of the risk profile being displayed on its B Corp public profile.

a) sets out the specific positive and meaningful impact the company intends to make on society or the environment, or both
b) has business relevance and is integrated into its strategy
c) is publicly available on the company’s webpage
d) is approved by the company’s highest governing body.

The company engages with its stakeholders and considers their interests in decision-making.

a) Workers of the company or its subsidiaries
b) Suppliers
c) Customers
d) Investors

The company’s stakeholder governance policy describes:
a) what it means to be a company with a stakeholder governance model
b) the criteria for identifying and prioritizing stakeholders, including a comprehensive map of the company's stakeholders
c) how decision-makers across the company consider stakeholders in decision-making related to (potential) positive and negative impacts
d) how the company delivers value to stakeholders through considering their interests
e) the mechanisms to encourage regular stakeholder engagement.

b) Suppliers

f) The local or global environment
The policy is approved by the highest governing body.
The policy is communicated to company workers and available for them to access.

a) Workers of the company or its subsidiaries
b) Suppliers

The materiality assessment:
a) covers the salient human rights issues and material environmental issues addressed in the B Lab Standard
b) covers topics relevant to the company and its stakeholders, but not addressed in the B Lab Standard
c) uses a double materiality or impact materiality approach. It cannot only assess financial materiality.
The company assesses topics based on their significance and sets a threshold to determine its material topics.

The company conducts a full materiality assessment at least every 36 months. Between full assessments, it also undertakes one interim review of materiality with a selection of its stakeholders, to update its material topics.
The highest governing body has oversight of the materiality assessment process and reviews the results.

The final outcome and the methodology the company used in its assessment are publicly available in the annual impact report or on the company’s webpage. The outcome may take the form of a materiality matrix or a list of identified material topics, plus a summary of stakeholder engagement processes.
The company identifies any material topics from its materiality assessment that are not addressed in the B Lab Standard.
The company sets at least one target per material topic it identifies.

The targets are:
a) specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART)
b) integrated into the company strategy
c) available to the public
d) approved by the highest governing body
The company assigns responsibility for achieving each target.
In the years after setting its targets, the company publicly reports its progress in its impact report or website.
Once the company has achieved a target for a material topic, it sets a new target that meets these Compliance Criteria.

The company documents decisions by the highest governing body that relate to dividends and stock buyback and which demonstrate how the company:
a) considered the interests of its stakeholders (not just shareholders)
b) evaluated stakeholder interests or balanced conflicting stakeholder interests.

The company considers impacts to the following stakeholders in relation to dividend and stock buyback decisions.
a) Workers of the company or its subsidiaries
b) Suppliers
c) Customers
d) Investors
e) The community where offices or facilities of the company, its subsidiaries, its suppliers, or its investments are located
f) The local or global environment
The company is publicly transparent on how decisions on dividends and stock buybacks are balanced with reinvestments in the company’s social and environmental performance.
The company publishes a grievance form on its webpage or has another easily accessible way for stakeholders to raise a grievance.

The grievance procedure explains:
a) grounds for accepting a grievance
b) grievance process steps and targeted deadlines for managing a grievance
c) how a resolution is facilitated
The company describes the processes and controls in place to protect stakeholders who raise grievances from any form of retaliation.

The company responds to stakeholder grievances by either:
a) regularly communicating each step in the resolution process and its outcome to the complainant, and confirming when the grievance has been resolved
b) explaining why it did not accept the issue as a grievance.
The company monitors and tracks grievances and prepares annual summaries of the status and subject of any grievances.
The company has an employee with well-defined responsibilities for managing grievances.

The company demonstrates the effectiveness of the grievance procedure by either:
a) recording evidence that a grievance has been resolved and closed
b) demonstrating that they have the appropriate grievance procedure in place (inclusive of tracking), where a company has had no grievances filed.
The company’s grievance procedure is available on its webpage in relevant languages or forms to ensure stakeholders can access it.

The grievance procedure explains:
a) grounds for accepting a grievance
b) grievance process steps and targeted deadlines for managing a grievance
c) how a resolution is facilitated
The grievance procedure states the processes and controls in place to protect stakeholders who raise grievances from any form of retaliation.

The company responds to stakeholder grievances by either:
a) regularly communicating each step in the resolution process and its outcome, and confirming when the grievance has been resolved
b) explaining why it did not accept the issue as a grievance.

c)  The company follows ethical guidelines when using sensitive marketing and public relations channels and practices.

All employees have an employment contract or offer letter meeting the following criteria.

b) It is signed by a company representative and the employee.

i) the name of the company
ii) the names of both signing parties
iii) the nature and place of the work
iv) working hours
v) the base wage
vi) any extra wage components
vii) the work start date
viii) the duration of the work
ix) conditions for termination.

c) Whether the company will pay the employee, and how much, when canceling their work after the deadline for reasons outside the company’s control.
